scenarios.title: The container that will not stay running
scenarios.summary: You build the image exactly as instructed and it succeeds. Then the container exits instantly with code 0 and no error message.

scenarios.title: Container is healthy, port is dead
scenarios.summary: The app logs that it is listening, docker ps shows the port mapped, and curl from your machine still refuses to connect.

scenarios.title: Multi-stage build that ships a 900 MB root container
scenarios.summary: Security rejected the image: it runs as root, weighs almost a gigabyte, and rebuilds everything on every code change. Fix all three without changing the app.

scenarios.title: COPY failed: file not found, and the file is right there
scenarios.summary: The build cannot find app.py, which is sitting next to the Dockerfile. Docker is looking in the build context, not where you think.

scenarios.title: The build-time variable that is empty at runtime
scenarios.summary: --build-arg APP_VERSION shows up during the build and is gone in the container. ARG and ENV live in different phases.

scenarios.title: The container is working and docker logs is empty
scenarios.summary: A long job produces no visible output until it exits, and nothing at all if it is killed. Stdout is being buffered.

scenarios.title: The bind mount that deleted your application
scenarios.summary: Add a volume and the container cannot find app.py, which is definitely in the image. The mount covered it up.

scenarios.title: You changed the code and the container runs the old version
scenarios.summary: Rebuild, rerun, same old behaviour. A cached layer and a container that was never replaced are both at fault.

scenarios.title: docker stop takes ten seconds and kills the job
scenarios.summary: The app handles SIGTERM cleanly and never gets the chance. One line of the Dockerfile puts a shell at PID 1.

scenarios.title: Two machines, same tag, different behaviour
scenarios.summary: Both hosts run internal/report:latest and behave differently. A tag is a mutable pointer, not an identity.

scenarios.title: The script that cannot find its own config file
scenarios.summary: The container fails to open config/settings.json, which is in the image. The working directory is not what the code assumes.

scenarios.title: No space left on device, and nothing is running
scenarios.summary: Docker is using 40 GB and docker ps shows almost nothing. Find the four hidden categories and reclaim safely.

scenarios.title: The API cannot reach the database container
scenarios.summary: Two running containers, one connects to db:5432 and gets name-not-known. The default bridge network provides no DNS.

scenarios.title: depends_on did not wait for the database
scenarios.summary: The API crashes on startup then recovers after retries. depends_on orders starts, it does not wait for readiness.

scenarios.title: Permission denied writing to a directory you own
scenarios.summary: The container cannot write to a bind mount you own, and running as root leaves root-owned files in your tree. UIDs must match.

scenarios.title: The healthcheck that reports healthy while the app is broken
scenarios.summary: One container serves 500s and shows healthy; another works and shows unhealthy. Both checks test the wrong thing.

scenarios.title: Exit code 137 and no error in the logs
scenarios.summary: A job dies mid-run with no traceback. Distinguish an OOM kill from an application crash and from docker stop.

scenarios.title: The image built on a laptop will not run on the server
scenarios.summary: exec format error on the servers, or twenty-times-slower emulation with no error at all. Build multi-arch images.

scenarios.title: Arguments to docker run are being ignored
scenarios.summary: docker run img --dry-run runs a full import, and you cannot get a shell. ENTRYPOINT and CMD are combined wrongly.

scenarios.title: The environment variable with four possible values
scenarios.summary: The .env says staging, Compose says staging, the container connects to production. Six sources, strictly ordered.

scenarios.title: The build fails on the CI runner and works on your laptop
scenarios.summary: pip install times out inside docker build though the runner has internet. The build does not inherit your shell's proxy.

scenarios.title: The secret you deleted is still in the image
scenarios.summary: A key was copied in then removed in a later layer. It is gone from the filesystem and trivially extractable from the image.

scenarios.title: Every CI build reinstalls every dependency
scenarios.summary: Local builds are fast, CI is eleven minutes every time. The layer cache lives on a builder that CI throws away.

scenarios.title: Thousands of defunct processes in a long-running container
scenarios.summary: A container leaks process-table entries until it cannot fork. PID 1 is your app, and it is not reaping children.

scenarios.title: The CI container that is secretly root on the host
scenarios.summary: Mounting the Docker socket into a build agent gives anyone who can run a build root on the host. Build without it.

scenarios.title: Containers cannot resolve DNS after a network change
scenarios.summary: Every container fails name resolution while the host is fine. Where the daemon reads resolv.conf, and when, is the key.

scenarios.title: The 1.2 GB image that should be 80 MB
scenarios.summary: A tiny service ships as 1.2 GB, pulled hundreds of times a day. Attribute the size to layers and cut it with multi-stage.

scenarios.title: Rolling deploys drop connections for ten seconds
scenarios.summary: Every deploy resets in-flight requests. Signal delivery and drain-versus-load-balancer ordering are both wrong.

scenarios.title: The container that thinks it has 64 CPUs
scenarios.summary: Limited to 2 CPUs, the app sizes a 128-thread pool from the host core count and throttles under load. Read the cgroup.

scenarios.title: The layer cache poisoned by apt-get update
scenarios.summary: A split apt update/install desynchronises via layer caching, installing missing or stale package versions. Combine and pin.

scenarios.title: CrashLoopBackOff on a pod that works locally
scenarios.summary: The same image runs fine under docker run. In the cluster it restarts forever. Read the pod's own account of what happened.

scenarios.title: Service returns connection refused, pods are Running
scenarios.summary: Every pod is ready and the Service exists, but curl through the Service times out. Nothing is in CrashLoop, so nothing looks wrong.

scenarios.title: Rollout stuck at 1/3 and the old pods are gone
scenarios.summary: A deploy is half finished, capacity is degraded, and kubectl rollout status just hangs. Three separate mistakes are fighting each other.

scenarios.title: ImagePullBackOff on an image that exists
scenarios.summary: The pod cannot pull an image you can pull by hand. A typo'd tag or a missing pull secret, not a broken registry.

scenarios.title: The pod stuck Pending with nowhere to go
scenarios.summary: No node can take the pod. It asks for more CPU than any node has, or a nodeSelector nothing matches.

scenarios.title: The ConfigMap value that never reaches the container
scenarios.summary: You updated the ConfigMap and the app still uses the old value. It was never wired into the pod spec.

scenarios.title: The pod that cannot read its own secret
scenarios.summary: CreateContainerConfigError because the key the pod asks for is not the key the Secret provides.

scenarios.title: kubectl points at the wrong cluster
scenarios.summary: 'No resources found' in one namespace, unfamiliar resources in another. The active context and namespace are not what you assume.

scenarios.title: The deployment applied cleanly and nothing changed
scenarios.summary: apply says configured or unchanged and the old pods keep running. Confirm the change actually reached the cluster.

scenarios.title: The container that exits before the probe can pass
scenarios.summary: A healthy app restarts every couple of minutes. A liveness probe hits an endpoint it does not serve.

scenarios.title: The label change that orphaned the pods
scenarios.summary: An immutable-selector error, or pods managed by nobody. Selector and template labels no longer agree.

scenarios.title: The namespace stuck in Terminating forever
scenarios.summary: Deleted an hour ago and still there. A resource carries a finalizer whose controller no longer exists.

scenarios.title: The service that routes to nothing
scenarios.summary: A Service with a ClusterIP and zero endpoints is a black hole. Its selector matches no pod labels.

scenarios.title: The pod that cannot talk after the network policy landed
scenarios.summary: DB connections and DNS both break once policies apply. Default-deny egress forgot to allow port 53.

scenarios.title: The rollout that got stuck halfway
scenarios.summary: Old pods still serving, one new pod not ready, rollout status hangs. A safe pause on a bad image, not a bug.

scenarios.title: The PVC that will not bind
scenarios.summary: The claim stays Pending and the pod with it. A missing StorageClass or an access mode the cluster cannot provide.

scenarios.title: The app that gets 403 from its own API server
scenarios.summary: Authenticated but not authorized. The ServiceAccount has no Role granting the verbs it calls.

scenarios.title: The pod that is slow because it is being throttled
scenarios.summary: Latency spikes while average CPU stays under the limit. A CPU limit throttles bursts within each CFS period.

scenarios.title: The ingress that returns 404 for a route that exists
scenarios.summary: The Service works on port-forward but the ingress host 404s. Wrong class, wrong backend port, or unmatched host.

scenarios.title: The job that runs forever and never completes
scenarios.summary: A Job retries a failing container endlessly and a CronJob overlaps its own runs. Bound retries, runtime and concurrency.

scenarios.title: The HPA that will not scale
scenarios.summary: TARGETS shows <unknown> and replicas never move. No CPU requests to compute a percentage against, or no metrics-server.

scenarios.title: The node that went NotReady and took the pods with it
scenarios.summary: One node stops reporting and its pods hang in limbo. Disk pressure, a dead kubelet, or lost control-plane contact.

scenarios.title: The DNS that resolves everything except the one service you need
scenarios.summary: Slow, flaky resolution under load. ndots:5 and the search path turn one lookup into several and flood CoreDNS.

scenarios.title: The pod that mounts a secret it should never see
scenarios.summary: A batch job is effectively cluster-admin and auto-mounts a powerful token. Cut the blast radius to least privilege.

scenarios.title: The eviction storm when the node ran out of memory
scenarios.summary: The important pods died and the memory hog survived. QoS class, set by your requests and limits, chose the victims.

scenarios.title: The StatefulSet that lost its data on restart
scenarios.summary: Replicas share one PVC and fight over it, or come back empty. Use volumeClaimTemplates for per-replica storage.

scenarios.title: The admission webhook that blocked the whole cluster
scenarios.summary: Every apply fails calling a webhook whose backend is down. failurePolicy Fail plus a broad scope wedged everything.

scenarios.title: The pods that all landed on one node
scenarios.summary: Three replicas, one node, no real HA. No enforced spread constraint, or one using a topology key the nodes lack.

scenarios.title: The taints and tolerations that left pods homeless
scenarios.summary: The GPU pod cannot land and an ordinary pod drifts onto the pricey nodes. Taints repel, tolerations permit, affinity attracts.

scenarios.title: The certificate that expired and no one noticed
scenarios.summary: Auto-renewal silently failed and the cert expired. Trace Certificate to CertificateRequest to Order to Issuer.

scenarios.title: The .gitignore that ignores nothing
scenarios.summary: You added the secrets file to .gitignore, but git still reports it as modified and it is already in the repository history.

scenarios.title: A merge conflict in a pipeline file
scenarios.summary: Two branches edited the same CI job. Resolve the conflict so the pipeline is correct, not just so git stops complaining.

scenarios.title: A hard reset ate this morning's work
scenarios.summary: Someone ran git reset --hard on the wrong branch and force-pushed. The commits are not in any branch. Get them back.

scenarios.title: The commits that vanished after I switched branches
scenarios.summary: You committed on a detached HEAD. Switching to main left those commits unnamed. Recover them from the reflog.

scenarios.title: The commit that succeeded and left the new files behind
scenarios.summary: git commit -am never stages untracked files. The message says you added them; the tree does not.

scenarios.title: checkout ate my uncommitted work
scenarios.summary: Forced checkout discarded edits that were never a commit. Stash or branch before you switch.

scenarios.title: Every commit is owned by someone else
scenarios.summary: Author identity unknown, or root@localhost. Set user.name and user.email at the right scope.

scenarios.title: Every file is modified and I did not change anything
scenarios.summary: Status is dirty from CRLF or filemode, not from real edits. Pin endings in .gitattributes.

scenarios.title: pull said already up to date, but the remote has new commits
scenarios.summary: git pull only updates the current branch's upstream. Fetch and switch to the branch you actually need.

scenarios.title: I cloned the repo and it is empty
scenarios.summary: Clone followed origin/HEAD onto an unused default branch. The files live on main.

scenarios.title: The submodule directory is empty after clone
scenarios.summary: A normal clone does not populate gitlinks. submodule update --init checks out the pinned SHA.

scenarios.title: I amended a commit that was already pushed
scenarios.summary: Amend rewrites the SHA. Push is non-fast-forward; force-with-lease or a follow-up commit instead.

scenarios.title: rebase turned my PR into a 40-commit mess
scenarios.summary: Rebase replays the wrong set of commits when the arguments are reversed. Abort and rebase onto main.

scenarios.title: stash pop destroyed my working tree
scenarios.summary: pop applies then drops. Recover from the stash reflog; prefer apply until the tree looks right.

scenarios.title: cherry-pick says empty and the bug is still there
scenarios.summary: The patch is already in the branch, or you picked a merge without -m. Skip or pick the original commit.

scenarios.title: force push erased a teammate's commit
scenarios.summary: --force sets the remote tip regardless. Recover the SHA from another clone; use --force-with-lease.

scenarios.title: git push went to the wrong remote branch
scenarios.summary: Local feature/billing tracks origin/main. Read status -sb and push -u origin HEAD.

scenarios.title: I deleted the file but git still has it
scenarios.summary: rm is not git rm. Tracked files ignore gitignore until git rm --cached is committed.

scenarios.title: --ours kept the wrong side of the merge
scenarios.summary: Whole-file ours/theirs drops the other side. During rebase the labels flip. Combine the hunks.

scenarios.title: Git LFS showed me a 130-byte image in production
scenarios.summary: Checkout without smudge ships the pointer file. git lfs pull and CI lfs: true.

scenarios.title: The pre-commit hook never runs
scenarios.summary: Hooks in the repo tree are not executed. Install into .git/hooks with +x, or set core.hooksPath.

scenarios.title: interactive rebase dropped a commit and I continued anyway
scenarios.summary: Deleting a pick line throws that commit off the new branch. Undo from reflog before you force-push.

scenarios.title: git bisect blamed a merge commit and I stopped looking
scenarios.summary: Bisect finds a boundary on this line of history. Walk the incoming parent or use -S for the real change.

scenarios.title: git filter-repo is the only way this secret leaves history
scenarios.summary: Removing the file from HEAD leaves the blob in old commits. Rewrite, rotate, and force-push every ref.

scenarios.title: worktree: branch already checked out
scenarios.summary: A branch can be HEAD in only one worktree. Add a second tree on a new branch; clones do not share objects.

scenarios.title: CI cloned --depth 1 and cannot describe or push tags
scenarios.summary: fetch-depth: 1 has no tag ancestry. Unshallow or fetch-depth: 0 for release jobs.

scenarios.title: rerere keeps applying a bad merge resolution
scenarios.summary: Recorded resolutions replay without asking. git rerere forget the path and resolve correctly.

scenarios.title: receive.denyCurrentBranch: the push to a non-bare repo
scenarios.summary: Pushing into a checkout is refused by default. Use a bare remote, not a human working tree.

scenarios.title: gc deleted the commit I was going to recover
scenarios.summary: Reflog expiry then prune drop unreachable objects. Branch the SHA immediately; do not gc --prune=now in a panic.

scenarios.title: signed commit, unsigned merge, broken verify
scenarios.summary: gpgsign fails without a key; merge commits are new unsigned objects. Sign with -S or SSH signing.

scenarios.title: Permission denied on a script you own
scenarios.summary: You wrote the script, you own the file, and the shell still refuses to run it. Then it fails a second time for a different reason.

scenarios.title: Address already in use, and nothing is using it
scenarios.summary: The service refuses to bind port 8080. The obvious command shows nothing listening. Find the process and the second failure behind it.

scenarios.title: The cron job that runs and does nothing
scenarios.summary: The backup job works when you run it by hand. Under cron it produces no output, no backup, and no error. Diagnose it without guessing.

scenarios.title: No space left on device, and df says half empty
scenarios.summary: Writes fail while df -h shows free space. The disk is out of inodes, not bytes; df -i tells the truth.

scenarios.title: command not found, but the program is installed
scenarios.summary: It runs by full path and dies by name. The binary's directory is not on PATH, and cron's PATH differs.

scenarios.title: You deleted the huge log and the disk is still full
scenarios.summary: rm removed the name but a process holds the file open, so the space is not freed. df and du disagree.

scenarios.title: The symlink that points at nothing
scenarios.summary: A link and its target both exist, yet access fails. A relative symlink resolves from the link's own directory.

scenarios.title: The environment variable the child process cannot see
scenarios.summary: echo shows the value; the program launched sees nothing. A shell variable is not exported until you say so.

scenarios.title: The directory you cannot enter
scenarios.summary: You own it, it is readable, and cd is denied. On directories x means traverse, r means list; they are not the same.

scenarios.title: sudo: command not found for a command that works
scenarios.summary: The tool runs as you and vanishes under sudo. sudo uses secure_path, not your PATH, on purpose.

scenarios.title: bad interpreter: the script with invisible carriage returns
scenarios.summary: A perfect-looking script fails with bad interpreter. CRLF line endings put a carriage return in the shebang.

scenarios.title: Argument list too long
scenarios.summary: rm *.log fails instantly on a huge directory. The shell expands the glob past the kernel's ARG_MAX.

scenarios.title: The process pinning a core at 100% CPU
scenarios.summary: The box is loud and slow. Find the runaway from a cold start, identify it properly, contain it least-disruptively.

scenarios.title: The process the kernel killed for you
scenarios.summary: A service vanished with exit 137 and no crash log. The OOM killer took it; the record is in dmesg, not the app.

scenarios.title: Too many open files
scenarios.summary: A busy service hits EMFILE with resources to spare. Decide between a leak and a limit that is simply too low.

scenarios.title: The systemd service that will not start
scenarios.summary: start returns, status says failed. Read the exit code and journal; fix Type, paths, user, and reload.

scenarios.title: The filesystem that went read-only
scenarios.summary: Even root cannot write. errors=remount-ro tripped on disk errors; check the FS and the hardware before remounting.

scenarios.title: The process that ignores your kill
scenarios.summary: kill does nothing and you reach for -9. Tell an ignored SIGTERM apart from an uninterruptible D-state process.

scenarios.title: The logs that grew until the disk was full
scenarios.summary: Rotation runs but the log keeps growing. The service holds the renamed inode open; use copytruncate or a reload.

scenarios.title: target is busy: the filesystem you cannot unmount
scenarios.summary: umount refuses because something holds the mount. Find every open file and stray cwd, then unmount cleanly.

scenarios.title: The files everyone creates with the wrong permissions
scenarios.summary: Shared files come out with the wrong group and no group-write. umask, setgid and default ACLs, not chmod 777.

scenarios.title: High load average while the CPUs sit idle
scenarios.summary: Load is 20 and the CPUs are idle. Load counts D-state I/O waiters; the bottleneck is storage, not compute.

scenarios.title: The server that looks out of memory but is not
scenarios.summary: free shows almost nothing free and nothing is dying. Read available, not free; the cache is reclaimable.

scenarios.title: The binary that fails silently, traced with strace
scenarios.summary: A program exits non-zero with no message. strace shows the failing syscall and its errno directly.

scenarios.title: Cannot assign requested address under load
scenarios.summary: A high-churn client runs out of ephemeral ports to TIME_WAIT. Reuse connections first, then tune the range.

scenarios.title: error while loading shared libraries
scenarios.summary: A binary cannot find a .so that exists on disk. Understand the linker search path and ldconfig, and soname changes.

scenarios.title: df says full, du says half - where did the space go
scenarios.summary: The filesystem is full but du cannot find it. Deleted-but-open files, or files shadowed under a mount point.

scenarios.title: The service that cannot bind port 80 without root
scenarios.summary: Binding a low port fails as non-root and the team runs it as root. Grant only CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE instead.

scenarios.title: Permission denied, and the permissions are perfect
scenarios.summary: ls -l looks right and access is still denied. A mandatory access control layer denies it; read the audit log.

scenarios.title: Connections dropped under load with resources free
scenarios.summary: The server drops connections while CPU and RAM idle. Kernel ceilings: listen backlog, conntrack, buffers.

scenarios.title: KeyError at 3 a.m.
scenarios.summary: A deploy script crashes with a bare traceback the moment an environment variable is absent. Make the failure useful instead of cryptic.

scenarios.title: Works on my machine, ModuleNotFoundError in CI
scenarios.summary: The script runs on your laptop and dies in the pipeline. The requirements file is the problem, and so is how the script is invoked.

scenarios.title: The automation that reports success after failing
scenarios.summary: A deployment wrapper calls three commands. The middle one fails, the script prints DONE and exits 0. This is how bad releases reach production.

scenarios.title: The inventory said Norway was down, and so was the node named on
scenarios.summary: YAML 1.1 turns NO/on/off/yes into booleans. Inventory loaders skip False names and roll True.

scenarios.title: The backup script works in the repo and writes nothing under cron
scenarios.summary: Relative Path('targets.txt') follows cwd, not the .py file. Cron's cwd is /.

scenarios.title: The watchdog is stuck and the pipeline slot is occupied for an hour
scenarios.summary: urlopen/requests without timeout= wait forever. Bound connect and read, fail the job.

scenarios.title: The sync job printed OK and the inventory is yesterday's 404 page
scenarios.summary: Transport success is not HTTP 2xx. raise_for_status; never turn a 404 HTML page into zero hosts.

scenarios.title: I forgot the flag and it deployed to production
scenarios.summary: argparse default=prod is a deploy. Require --env and a second flag for production.

scenarios.title: The job ran, CloudWatch has one line that says done, and we cannot grep it
scenarios.summary: print() has no time, level, or fields, and it breaks jq on stdout. Log to stderr.

scenarios.title: The agent upgrade skipped 1.10 because 1.9 was newer
scenarios.summary: String compare says '1.10' < '1.9'. Parse integers or packaging.version, then decide.

scenarios.title: jq says parse error and kubectl said the object was fine
scenarios.summary: check_output captured a warning on stdout with the JSON. Parse only the document; log on stderr.

scenarios.title: ./cleanup.py dies on the jump host and runs on your laptop
scenarios.summary: #!/usr/bin/env python is not python3. The shebang is the production interpreter.

scenarios.title: The rendered nginx config has server_name ; and nginx still started
scenarios.summary: Missing {{hostname}} became empty. StrictUndefined / KeyError; do not write a hole.

scenarios.title: The Python config from the other team deleted the working directory
scenarios.summary: eval/exec/yaml.load/pickle of a settings file is code execution. ast.literal_eval or JSON.

scenarios.title: The audit said 30 IAM keys and the account has 400
scenarios.summary: The first page is a page. Follow next/NextToken/Link until it is gone.

scenarios.title: The retry loop turned a 404 into a 20-minute outage
scenarios.summary: Retries are for 429/502, not for 404. Classify before sleep; cap wall time.

scenarios.title: verify=False is still in the healthcheck we copied to production
scenarios.summary: An unverified HTTPS canary is a TCP check. Pass cafile; grep the org for verify=False.

scenarios.title: The node went NotReady because we crashed while rewriting kubelet config
scenarios.summary: open(path,'w') truncates first. Write a sibling temp file and os.replace.

scenarios.title: Two crons ran the drain and the node was cordoned twice into a deadlock
scenarios.summary: A 8-minute job on a 5-minute cron overlaps. flock or concurrencyPolicy: Forbid.

scenarios.title: The exception handler logged the Authorization header to Slack
scenarios.summary: repr(request) includes the bearer token. Log URL and error class; redact headers.

scenarios.title: The cert-expiry cron said 12 days left and the cert died at midnight UTC
scenarios.summary: datetime.now() is naive local time. Parse Z as UTC and compare timezone-aware clocks.

scenarios.title: Kubernetes sent SIGTERM and the job wrote a half-empty dump anyway
scenarios.summary: Uncaught SIGTERM is a mid-file crash. Handle it, stop the loop, exit 1, publish atomically.

scenarios.title: Parallel rollouts: three nodes failed and the script printed SUCCESS
scenarios.summary: Thread exceptions live on the Future until .result(). Collect failures; exit non-zero.

scenarios.title: Fifty crons woke up at :00 and the API spent 10 minutes saying 429
scenarios.summary: Honour Retry-After, add jitter, stagger crontab. Immediate retry is a thundering herd.

scenarios.title: The deploy script imported json and got our helper instead of the stdlib
scenarios.summary: cwd is on sys.path. A local json.py shadows the stdlib under systemd WorkingDirectory.

scenarios.title: Every hourly run created another DNS record named app
scenarios.summary: POST every cron is 720 records a month. Lookup by natural key; upsert or no-op.

scenarios.title: The cleanup glob followed a symlink and wiped /var/lib/app
scenarios.summary: Path.glob('**/*') descends through scratch/data -> /var/lib/app. Skip symlinks; prefix-check.

scenarios.title: node-exporter scraped a textfile of zero bytes and Grafana said the box was gone
scenarios.summary: Empty .prom plus exit 0 hides the outage. Publish app_up 0, stable labels, atomic replace.

scenarios.title: Terraform's external data source got INFO starting instead of JSON
scenarios.summary: Stdout is the protocol. Logs on stderr; one JSON object on stdout; stringly-typed for terraform.

scenarios.title: The security gate timed out and the pipeline shipped anyway
scenarios.summary: except Exception: return 0 is fail-open. If the scanner did not run, do not deploy.

scenarios.title: The backup script that deletes the wrong thing
scenarios.summary: An unquoted variable turns one path with a space into two arguments. The script reports success while doing something else entirely.

scenarios.title: Exit code 0 on a pipeline that failed
scenarios.summary: A CI step greps a log that was never produced. Every command in the chain failed and the job still went green.

scenarios.title: The script that leaks a lock file forever
scenarios.summary: It creates a lock and a temp dir, then exits early on error and leaves both behind. Every later run refuses to start.

scenarios.title: The if that is always true
scenarios.summary: [ $STATUS = 200 ] explodes on empty and globs inside [ ]. Quote or use [[ and -eq.

scenarios.title: 08 is not a number, and 1+1 is 11
scenarios.summary: Leading zeros are octal in $(( )). String + is concatenation. Force base 10.

scenarios.title: The env file I ran did nothing
scenarios.summary: ./env.sh exports in a child. source / . runs in this shell so REGION survives.

scenarios.title: The script cds and then I am still in the old directory
scenarios.summary: cd in a child or pipe cannot change the parent cwd. Source, or use absolute paths.

scenarios.title: rm *.log deleted a file named *.log
scenarios.summary: Unmatched globs pass through as the pattern. nullglob or an array loop is the safe delete.

scenarios.title: read ate the leading spaces and the last line
scenarios.summary: Default IFS trims; read exits 1 at EOF without a newline. IFS= read -r and || [[ -n $line ]].

scenarios.title: The heredoc that leaked the password and broke the script
scenarios.summary: Unquoted <<EOF expands $HOME and secrets. Quote the delimiter or escape the dollars you need literal.

scenarios.title: set -e did not stop the script
scenarios.summary: errexit is off in if / || / while conditions. Handle critical failures explicitly; keep set -e as a backstop.

scenarios.title: $0 is the wrapper, not this file
scenarios.summary: Sourced libraries that dirname $0 look next to the caller. Use BASH_SOURCE[0] for the current file.

scenarios.title: IFS=, turned every line into one field
scenarios.summary: Global IFS changes every unquoted split. Prefix IFS=, to read, join in a subshell.

scenarios.title: The while loop forgot every variable
scenarios.summary: find | while read runs in a subshell; counters die. Process substitution keeps the loop in this shell.

scenarios.title: ${arr[1]} is empty and arr=foo still looks like an array
scenarios.summary: files=*.txt is a string. Parentheses make arrays; echo $arr is only [0]; use "${arr[@]}".

scenarios.title: set -u vs optional arguments
scenarios.summary: $1 is unbound with zero args. Check $# and ${2:-latest}; keep nounset on.

scenarios.title: local foo=bar bash considers unset
scenarios.summary: local a=1 b=$a expands b first; local n=$(false) hides the failure. Split local and assign.

scenarios.title: xargs ran the command twice on one filename
scenarios.summary: Default xargs splits on spaces. find -print0 | xargs -0, or find -exec ... {} +.

scenarios.title: The background job I forgot to wait for
scenarios.summary: backup &; exit 0 is green while the child fails. Save $! and wait; accumulate status.

scenarios.title: getopts swallowed the argument after -f
scenarios.summary: getopts fv does not take a file for -f. Put : after letters that need args; shift OPTIND.

scenarios.title: Process substitution hid the curl exit code
scenarios.summary: jq < <(curl) loses HTTP failure. Write the body with -o and -w '%{http_code}', then parse.

scenarios.title: nameref and ${!var} pointed at the wrong thing
scenarios.summary: declare -n ref=$1 collides or injects. Validate identifiers; never eval untrusted names.

scenarios.title: trap DEBUG and ERR that never fired
scenarios.summary: ERR traps need set -E to run in functions. Cleanup stays on EXIT; pair errexit with errtrace.

scenarios.title: lastpipe, coproc, and the fifo that deadlocked
scenarios.summary: Opening a FIFO for read blocks until a writer. exec 3<> or drain the coproc; pipe buffers are finite.

scenarios.title: Associative array keys that look like numbers
scenarios.summary: Indexed arrays treat 08 as octal 8. declare -A first; keys are strings; iteration order is not sorted.

scenarios.title: eval constructed a command from untrusted input
scenarios.summary: eval "docker run $FLAGS" runs $(touch pwned). Build argv arrays; never eval user flags.

scenarios.title: flock: the lock that did not lock
scenarios.summary: rm the lock file then flock a new inode. Hold an fd on a stable local file for the process lifetime.

scenarios.title: It works in bash and dies under /bin/sh
scenarios.summary: dash rejects pipefail, arrays, and [[. Either #!/usr/bin/env bash or rewrite to POSIX.

scenarios.title: set -x printed the secret in CI
scenarios.summary: xtrace expands curl -u admin:$PASSWORD into the log. set +x around secrets; keep them off argv.

scenarios.title: Job control: SIGPIPE, yes | head, and a pipeline that lies
scenarios.summary: pipefail treats yes|head as 141. Save PIPESTATUS; allow SIGPIPE only for known early-close consumers.

scenarios.title: Terraform will not even initialise
scenarios.summary: Four small mistakes in one config: a bad provider block, an undeclared variable, a wrong reference, and a type error. No cloud account required.

scenarios.title: Renaming one item destroys five resources
scenarios.summary: The config uses count over a list. Removing the first element makes the plan recreate everything after it. Fix the addressing, not the list.

scenarios.title: The plan wants to destroy production
scenarios.summary: Someone changed a resource by hand and someone else renamed it in code. Reconcile state and reality until plan shows no destroys.

scenarios.title: Plan says `dev` while you are holding `prod.tfvars`
scenarios.summary: prod.tfvars is not auto-loaded; only terraform.tfvars / *.auto.tfvars are. Plan uses defaults until -var-file.

scenarios.title: `module.web.addr` does not exist
scenarios.summary: Root interpolates a child attribute that was never output. Locals inside the module stay private.

scenarios.title: `templatefile` cannot find a file that is in the module
scenarios.summary: templatefile path is resolved from cwd, not the module. Use path.module.

scenarios.title: Terraform refuses to run: core version
scenarios.summary: required_version is newer than the installed CLI; init never reaches providers.

scenarios.title: Staging workspace looks empty after a successful apply
scenarios.summary: Applied in default, then selected staging. Local state is a different file, not a relabel.

scenarios.title: CI picked a different provider version than your laptop
scenarios.summary: .terraform.lock.hcl was not committed; CI floated a different provider version.

scenarios.title: The database password is in the CI log
scenarios.summary: Password in terraform output / CI logs. sensitive redacts CLI; the value stays in state.

scenarios.title: They ran Terraform in the other stack
scenarios.summary: Two roots in one repo; they applied the wrong stack. Use -chdir.

scenarios.title: The data source has nothing to read
scenarios.summary: data.local_file / remote state points at a missing file or empty outputs.

scenarios.title: The file is already there; Terraform wants to create it
scenarios.summary: Object exists, state is empty, plan wants to create. terraform import the address.

scenarios.title: Renaming a resource destroys it
scenarios.summary: Renaming a resource address is destroy/create until moved {}.

scenarios.title: `state rm` made the next apply recreate the resource
scenarios.summary: state rm unmanages; next apply recreates. Import it back, do not rm to silence a plan.

scenarios.title: `ignore_changes` hid the drift permanently
scenarios.summary: lifecycle ignore_changes makes plan empty while reality is wrong.

scenarios.title: Yesterday's plan is not today's: the module tracks `main`
scenarios.summary: Module source tracks main; yesterday's plan is not today's. Pin a tag or SHA.

scenarios.title: `dynamic "ingress"` emitted nothing (then exploded on a duplicate key)
scenarios.summary: dynamic for_each empty is N=0; duplicate keys explode. Key on a unique attribute.

scenarios.title: Remote state outputs are empty (wrong key)
scenarios.summary: terraform_remote_state reads the wrong workspace or key; outputs are empty.

scenarios.title: The precondition failed with the message `invalid`
scenarios.summary: lifecycle.precondition inverted or error_message useless. Fix the boolean and the text.

scenarios.title: `create_before_destroy` plus a name that can only exist once
scenarios.summary: create_before_destroy plus a unique name cannot exist twice during replacement.

scenarios.title: S3 backend, no lock: last apply wins
scenarios.summary: S3 backend without DynamoDB/use_lockfile: concurrent applies, last writer wins.

scenarios.title: The private key is in `terraform.tfstate`
scenarios.summary: random_password / tls_private_key are plaintext in tfstate. What belongs in TF vs SSM.

scenarios.title: `-target` left the stack half-updated
scenarios.summary: apply -target left the stack half-updated; the next full plan is the rest of the diff.

scenarios.title: Provider block inside the child module; alias never arrives
scenarios.summary: provider {} inside a child module blocks passed aliases. Root configures; child consumes.

scenarios.title: `for_each` depends on a value unknown until apply
scenarios.summary: for_each over a value unknown until apply cannot be planned. Iterate a known variable.

scenarios.title: Cycle: each file points at the other
scenarios.summary: Two resources reference each other. Break the cycle with locals for static values.

scenarios.title: Everything replaces because of `replace_triggered_by` and `timestamp()`
scenarios.summary: replace_triggered_by a timestamp/nonce recreates the resource every plan.

scenarios.title: `jq` on state without `state mv`: serial mismatch
scenarios.summary: jq-edited state without state mv: serial/checksum mismatch. Restore; use state mv.

scenarios.title: Backend migrated halfway: two state files
scenarios.summary: init without -migrate-state created an empty new state beside the old one.

scenarios.title: AccessDenied on a bucket you own
scenarios.summary: You create a user, attach a policy that looks correct, and every S3 call is denied. The policy is missing something specific.

scenarios.title: The instance nobody can reach
scenarios.summary: An EC2 instance is running and healthy in the console. SSH and HTTP both hang. Four different layers could be at fault.

scenarios.title: CI cannot assume the deploy role
scenarios.summary: The role has the right permissions and the pipeline still gets AccessDenied on sts:AssumeRole. Two policies must agree and only one does.

scenarios.title: Allow looks wide open. Every call is still denied.
scenarios.summary: Identity Allow matches, but a leftover Deny also matches. Deny wins; simulator says explicitDeny.

scenarios.title: AccessDenied in us-east-1 for a secret that exists
scenarios.summary: Resource lives in eu-west-1; the job defaults to us-east-1. Looks like IAM; it is a region miss.

scenarios.title: The instance profile is attached and the app still uses yesterday's keys
scenarios.summary: IMDS is healthy; the process still signs with env keys because the SDK prefers the environment.

scenarios.title: The security group allows itself, and the instances are not in it
scenarios.summary: SG allows itself but the instances are in a different group. Self-reference is not 'open to the app'.

scenarios.title: IAM allows GetObject. The bucket policy does not.
scenarios.summary: Identity policy allows GetObject; the bucket policy Deny still wins.

scenarios.title: The condition that never matches
scenarios.summary: Condition key/operator never matches (literal * or aws:username on a role). Implicit deny.

scenarios.title: S3 is allowed. The object is encrypted. GetObject is still denied.
scenarios.summary: S3 allowed; object is SSE-KMS. GetObject needs kms:Decrypt on the CMK.

scenarios.title: IMDS works on the host and 401s in the container
scenarios.summary: IMDSv2 hop limit 1 drops the token PUT from a container. Host curl works; the task has no creds.

scenarios.title: CloudTrail says ListBuckets. The policy says ListBucket.
scenarios.summary: aws s3 ls with no bucket is ListAllMyBuckets, not ListBucket. CloudTrail names the real API.

scenarios.title: AdministratorAccess, and the simulator still says implicitDeny
scenarios.summary: AdministratorAccess plus a developer permissions boundary. The ceiling wins.

scenarios.title: You are admin. The organisation is not.
scenarios.summary: Member-account admin cannot override an SCP Deny. IAM edits in the child change nothing.

scenarios.title: The security group is open. The VPC endpoint is not.
scenarios.summary: SG is open; the gateway endpoint policy allows only another bucket. S3 from the VPC is denied.

scenarios.title: The database times out on 3306. The instance is fine.
scenarios.summary: RDS SG still allows the old ECS group on 3306. The API uses a new SG; SYN times out.

scenarios.title: The instance is healthy. The load balancer says it is not.
scenarios.summary: EC2 2/2 passed; target group checks the wrong port or path. Instance healthy, target not.

scenarios.title: The task role can read S3. The image never starts.
scenarios.summary: taskRole vs executionRole swapped. ECR pull uses execution; app S3 uses task.

scenarios.title: The bucket policy is public. Block Public Access is on.
scenarios.summary: Bucket policy is public; Block Public Access still 403s. BPA is not a suggestion.

scenarios.title: GetSecretValue denied by a policy you did not attach to the role
scenarios.summary: IAM allows GetSecretValue; the secret resource policy Denies everyone except an old role.

scenarios.title: NACL allows 443 in. The reply never comes back.
scenarios.summary: Custom NACLs are stateless. Allowing 443 both ways still drops ephemeral return traffic.

scenarios.title: The service can assume this role from any account
scenarios.summary: Service principal can AssumeRole from any account. Bind SourceArn/SourceAccount.

scenarios.title: AssumeRole succeeded. Every API call after it is denied.
scenarios.summary: AssumeRole succeeded; a session policy intersected the session down to GetObject.

scenarios.title: The pod's service account is not the one the role trusts
scenarios.summary: IRSA trust sub does not match the pod serviceaccount. AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity fails.

scenarios.title: IAM allows kms:Decrypt. The key policy does not.
scenarios.summary: IAM allows kms:Decrypt; the CMK key policy does not name the role. KMS still denies.

scenarios.title: Cross-account GetObject dies on a CMK you do not own
scenarios.summary: Cross-account GetObject: bucket policy and IAM allow; the CMK policy never named the reader.

scenarios.title: Lambda in a VPC times out talking to AWS
scenarios.summary: Lambda in private subnets, no NAT, no interface endpoints. AWS APIs time out.

scenarios.title: CloudFront 403: leftover OAI, new OAC
scenarios.summary: Distribution uses OAC; bucket policy still names a deleted OAI. CloudFront 403.

scenarios.title: The vendor cannot assume the role without ExternalId
scenarios.summary: Vendor trust is right; sts:ExternalId is still the staging value.

scenarios.title: You updated IAM. Nobody updated the resource policy.
scenarios.summary: Cross-account SQS/S3/KMS needs identity AND resource policy. Only one side was updated.

scenarios.title: The build is green and the tests never ran
scenarios.summary: Six weeks of passing builds, and a failing test printed in every single log. Three lines make failure impossible to report.

scenarios.title: Works on the controller, fails on the agent
scenarios.summary: The job fails half the time and re-running fixes it. Nothing is random: it depends entirely on which executor picked it up.

scenarios.title: The pipeline that never finishes
scenarios.summary: Nine hours in, holding three executors, with every other job queued behind it. Find what it is waiting for and make it impossible.

scenarios.title: The build that sits in the queue forever
scenarios.summary: Pending 'waiting for next available executor' while agents sit idle. The job asks for a label no agent advertises.

scenarios.title: The build that sees last week's files
scenarios.summary: A packaging job ships files deleted weeks ago. Workspaces are reused and never cleaned between runs.

scenarios.title: Permission denied running a script from the repo
scenarios.summary: ./build.sh runs on your laptop and fails in Jenkins. The execute bit was not preserved in git.

scenarios.title: The variable that is empty in the shell step
scenarios.summary: An env var is empty in sh, and switching to double quotes leaks a token into the log. Groovy vs shell expansion.

scenarios.title: The Jenkinsfile that will not compile
scenarios.summary: A wall of Groovy errors before any stage runs. Declarative and scripted syntax were mixed and steps misplaced.

scenarios.title: credentials(...) fails with 'Could not find credentials'
scenarios.summary: The credential exists in the UI and the job cannot find it. The ID does not match, character for character.

scenarios.title: The parameters that are not there on the first build
scenarios.summary: New parameters are ignored on the first run and empty values slip through. Parameter defs register only after a build.

scenarios.title: archiveArtifacts finds nothing to archive
scenarios.summary: The file is created but no artifact appears. The archive pattern is resolved relative to the workspace root.

scenarios.title: Pushes to the repo do not trigger a build
scenarios.summary: The job only runs when clicked. It has no trigger, and the webhook route fails silently if Jenkins is unreachable.

scenarios.title: Parallel stages overwrite each other's files
scenarios.summary: Parallel build variants ship the wrong binary intermittently. The branches share one workspace and race on filenames.

scenarios.title: The shared library that will not load
scenarios.summary: deployHelper() fails with No such DSL method though the library exists. It is never imported with @Library.

scenarios.title: The stage that never runs, and the one that always does
scenarios.summary: A when-branch-main deploy never runs and a failure-only cleanup runs every time. Wrong branch string, wrong construct.

scenarios.title: Files vanish between stages on different agents
scenarios.summary: Build on one agent, deploy on another, and the artifact is gone. Each agent has its own workspace; use stash/unstash.

scenarios.title: The Docker-agent build writes root-owned files
scenarios.summary: A container agent leaves root-owned files that wedge later builds. Run the container as the Jenkins agent user.

scenarios.title: The matrix build that runs one combination
scenarios.summary: A 3x2 matrix runs a single cell and ignores the axis values. Single-value axes collapse the product.

scenarios.title: The retry that hammers a flaky step to death
scenarios.summary: retry(100) with no backoff or timeout calls a struggling service a hundred times in seconds. Bound and back off.

scenarios.title: Test results never appear in the trend graph
scenarios.summary: Tests run but the trend is empty and failures are not listed. Wrong junit path, and publishing skipped on failure.

scenarios.title: The downstream job that ignores the version you passed
scenarios.summary: An upstream build triggers a deploy that always ships 'latest'. Parameters were never passed to the build step.

scenarios.title: The build server that fills its own disk and stops
scenarios.summary: The controller stops scheduling: disk full of two years of build history. Nothing was ever set to discard old builds.

scenarios.title: The pipeline rejected by the script security sandbox
scenarios.summary: After an upgrade, unchanged Groovy fails with RejectedAccessException. Use sandbox-safe pipeline steps, not approvals.

scenarios.title: The nightly job that misses runs and doubles up
scenarios.summary: A cron job overlaps itself and every job fires at exactly 02:00. Prevent concurrency and use H to spread load.

scenarios.title: The agent that keeps going offline
scenarios.summary: An agent drops several times a day with ping timeouts. It is OOM-killed, clock-drifted, and overcommitted, not networked.

scenarios.title: The deploy that cannot be undone
scenarios.summary: In-place overwrite destroys the previous release and records nothing. Rebuild deploy around versioned releases and a symlink.

scenarios.title: A pull request build that can steal your credentials
scenarios.summary: Fork PRs build automatically with deploy secrets in scope, so a PR can print them. Separate trusted and untrusted paths.

scenarios.title: The 900-line Jenkinsfile nobody dares change
scenarios.summary: One file, eight jobs of conditional sprawl and copy-paste. Data-drive the target and extract steps to a shared library.

scenarios.title: The pipeline that deploys before the tests finish
scenarios.summary: wait:false and split jobs let deploy run while tests are still going. Make the ordering structural and propagate failure.

scenarios.title: The build passes locally and fails only in the pipeline
scenarios.summary: A date test and an order-dependent test are green locally, red in CI. Pin the environment and make tests independent.

scenarios.title: The fix that keeps undoing itself
scenarios.summary: You scaled the deployment during an incident. Four minutes later it was back. Something is fighting you, and it was installed on purpose.

scenarios.title: Deleted from git, still running in production
scenarios.summary: A resource removed three months ago is still in the cluster, and Argo says Synced. Meanwhile every fresh install fails on ordering.

scenarios.title: The application that redeploys every three minutes
scenarios.summary: 4,812 syncs in ten days with no commits. Two controllers disagree about who owns a field, and pods restart all day because of it.

scenarios.title: The merge that never reached the cluster
scenarios.summary: Git merged; the cluster still runs last week's image. Auto-sync, prune, and selfHeal are off.

scenarios.title: The Application that syncs nothing from a full repo
scenarios.summary: spec.source.path points at a missing or empty directory. Argo is Synced with zero resources.

scenarios.title: Tracking main locally, shipping staging in the cluster
scenarios.summary: Application targetRevision is staging or a stale SHA while the laptop tracks main.

scenarios.title: Destination shop, live objects in default
scenarios.summary: metadata.namespace in the manifest wins over destination.namespace; workloads land in default.

scenarios.title: The repo is fine; the project refuses it
scenarios.summary: AppProject sourceRepos or destinations block the git URL, cluster, or namespace.

scenarios.title: Nested overlays exist in git and never sync
scenarios.summary: directory.recurse is false, so nested env/ overlays never become desired state.

scenarios.title: values.yaml bumped the tag; the cluster did not
scenarios.summary: Application helm.parameters override values.yaml, so the image tag in git never applies.

scenarios.title: OutOfSync extras that git never declared
scenarios.summary: A kubectl-applied object lacks Argo tracking labels and shows as an extra/orphan.

scenarios.title: Destination namespace does not exist
scenarios.summary: Dest namespace does not exist until CreateNamespace or a Namespace manifest.

scenarios.title: Manual sync refused during a deny window
scenarios.summary: An AppProject deny window blocks auto and manual sync while the fix sits on main.

scenarios.title: Git changed; Argo skipped the object on purpose
scenarios.summary: reconcile: skip or IgnoreExtraneous hides an object so git changes never apply.

scenarios.title: The Helm pre-install Job that never runs on the upgrade
scenarios.summary: helm.sh/hook: pre-install runs only on first install; later syncs skip migrations.

scenarios.title: ApplicationSet never created the EU app
scenarios.summary: ApplicationSet generator glob or cluster selector never emits one cluster; that app is missing.

scenarios.title: Local user can see the app and cannot sync it
scenarios.summary: policy.csv grants get but not sync. Argo RBAC is not Kubernetes RBAC.

scenarios.title: Multi-source ref name does not match $values
scenarios.summary: Multi-source ref name does not match $values; Helm never mounts the git values file.

scenarios.title: Git moved; Argo's compare cache did not
scenarios.summary: Soft refresh still renders cached manifests; hard refresh invalidates repo-server cache.

scenarios.title: Prod Application pointed at the dev overlay
scenarios.summary: Prod Application path is overlays/dev so prod image and replica patches never apply.

scenarios.title: Immutable Service field: apply is not enough
scenarios.summary: Immutable Service field cannot be patched; Replace=true lets the controller recreate it.

scenarios.title: Application deletion hangs on the finalizer
scenarios.summary: Application deletion hangs on resources-finalizer; a child will not die.

scenarios.title: Parent app is Synced; the child Application was never created
scenarios.summary: Parent is Synced; child Application CR was never rendered (path/recurse/wave).

scenarios.title: Destination server URL does not match any cluster secret
scenarios.summary: destination.server/name does not match the cluster Secret. Unknown cluster.

scenarios.title: Private repo, 401, credentials Secret does not match the URL
scenarios.summary: Private repo 401: HTTPS vs SSH, helm vs git type, or URL mismatch on the creds Secret.

scenarios.title: Custom resource applied before the CRD is established
scenarios.summary: CR applied before the CRD is Established. Put CRDs on an earlier sync wave.

scenarios.title: Git is quiet; the app is Progressing forever
scenarios.summary: Git is quiet; Health Progressing: controller timeout or a workload that never becomes Ready.

scenarios.title: Phantom diffs from last-applied vs server-side apply
scenarios.summary: Phantom diffs from last-applied vs server-side apply — not a two-controller sync loop.

scenarios.title: Sync failed and nobody was notified
scenarios.summary: Trigger watches on-sync-succeeded so a Failed sync never fires the webhook.

scenarios.title: ApplicationSet rolled the bad app to every cluster
scenarios.summary: applicationsSync: sync with no RollingSync ships a bad template to every cluster at once.

scenarios.title: The workflow that never runs
scenarios.summary: No run, no error, no annotation. Four separate reasons GitHub is ignoring your file, and not one of them produces a log.

scenarios.title: The cache that never hits and the secret that is not there
scenarios.summary: Caching was added and builds got slower. Fork pull requests fail with an empty credential. Both problems report themselves as success.

scenarios.title: The deploy job that cannot get credentials
scenarios.summary: Keyless AWS auth fails with AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity denied. Three faults in the identity chain, plus two a security review would block.

scenarios.title: The workflow only runs when I click the button
scenarios.summary: on: workflow_dispatch replaced push; it does not add to a default. List every event you need.

scenarios.title: paths: I changed the app and CI did not run
scenarios.summary: Path filters skip the workflow; required checks then wait forever. Include real app paths and the workflow file.

scenarios.title: The matrix cancelled the good jobs
scenarios.summary: fail-fast defaults to true. One cell fails, siblings cancel. Set fail-fast: false to see the rest.

scenarios.title: checkout tested the merge commit, not my branch
scenarios.summary: pull_request checkout is a merge into the base. Log github.sha vs head.sha; reproduce with merge locally.

scenarios.title: GITHUB_TOKEN cannot push the release tag
scenarios.summary: contents: read cannot git push. Grant contents: write on the releasing job only.

scenarios.title: secrets.* is empty in env: but I set the secret
scenarios.summary: Secret names are case-sensitive; environment secrets need environment:. Map into env: and test -n.

scenarios.title: needs: skipped the deploy because the tests were skipped
scenarios.summary: Skipped needs are not success(). Use always() and needs.x.result, or stop skipping the test job.

scenarios.title: upload-artifact says no files found
scenarios.summary: Wrong path, and the next job is a new VM. Upload the real glob; download-artifact in the consumer.

scenarios.title: concurrency cancelled the deploy I needed
scenarios.summary: cancel-in-progress is right for PR CI and wrong for production. Queue prod; cancel feature branches.

scenarios.title: The reusable workflow could not see the input
scenarios.summary: with: keys must match workflow_call inputs; secrets go in secrets: not with:. Schema is strict.

scenarios.title: The composite action did not run my setup
scenarios.summary: Composite run: steps require shell:. Use github.action_path and GITHUB_OUTPUT for outputs.

scenarios.title: restore-keys hit a cache from another OS
scenarios.summary: Short restore-keys prefix-match stale or foreign caches. Hash lockfiles; never restore-keys: runner.os- alone.

scenarios.title: The self-hosted runner job sat queued forever
scenarios.summary: runs-on labels are AND. A missing gpu label queues forever. Match live runner labels.

scenarios.title: The environment gate waited for a reviewer who did not exist
scenarios.summary: Required reviewers left the org; environment secrets are invisible without environment:.

scenarios.title: if: failure() never ran because the job was skipped
scenarios.summary: Step failure() is previous steps in this job. continue-on-error makes the job succeed. Notify in a needs job.

scenarios.title: matrix include replaced the whole matrix
scenarios.summary: include without base arrays is only those rows. Cartesian product plus include/exclude; empty matrix is a silent pass.

scenarios.title: The artifact expired before the manual deploy
scenarios.summary: download-artifact without run-id looks at this run. Pass the build run-id; raise retention or rebuild.

scenarios.title: Dependabot PRs cannot read secrets and cannot trigger workflows
scenarios.summary: Dependabot pull_request is untrusted. Do not use pull_request_target to grab NPM_TOKEN; use public CI or Dependabot registries.

scenarios.title: pull_request_target checked out the fork and kept the secrets
scenarios.summary: Privileged event plus checkout of head.sha runs attacker code with base secrets. Never combine them.

scenarios.title: secrets: inherit passed production into a docs workflow
scenarios.summary: inherit is every caller secret, not the callee schema. Map explicit keys; ban printenv in callees.

scenarios.title: OIDC worked in CI.yml and failed in the reusable workflow
scenarios.summary: job_workflow_ref replaces ref: in sub. Trust the callee workflow SHA, and keep id-token: write on that job.

scenarios.title: The action tag moved and CI started shipping malware-shaped code
scenarios.summary: uses: ...@v4 and @master are mutable. Pin full SHAs; let Dependabot bump them.

scenarios.title: The PR title became a bash command
scenarios.summary: ${{ github.event.pull_request.title }} in run: is interpolated as code. Pass untrusted fields via env:.

scenarios.title: The cache grew to 10 GB and every job missed
scenarios.summary: Unbounded paths and github.sha in the key never hit and evict useful caches. Hash lockfiles; split by tool.

scenarios.title: Merge queue says required check is missing
scenarios.summary: on: pull_request does not run on merge_group. Add the event and keep the check name identical.

scenarios.title: persist-credentials left a GITHUB_TOKEN in a downstream container
scenarios.summary: checkout stores the token in .git/config. Disable persist on build jobs; dockerignore .git.

scenarios.title: The reusable workflow could not write checks, so the PR stayed yellow
scenarios.summary: Central CI posts checks on the wrong repo or under a different job name. Name the caller job to match the ruleset.

scenarios.title: The site is down, but ping works
scenarios.summary: The host answers ICMP and the service is healthy, and the user still cannot load the page. Learn which tool tests which layer.

scenarios.title: Certificate errors behind the corporate proxy
scenarios.summary: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED, and the team's fix is curl -k. Trust the interception properly instead of switching off verification.

scenarios.title: Small requests work, large ones hang forever
scenarios.summary: Under 1400 bytes always succeeds, above it never returns. Every layer reports success while a router silently drops your packets.

scenarios.title: Connection refused in staging, timeout in production
scenarios.summary: RST means nothing is listening; silence means the packet never came back. Same 'down' ticket, two toolboxes.

scenarios.title: The dashboard is up on the box, curl from my laptop says connection refused
scenarios.summary: localhost:8080 is not http://host on port 80. Listen where the URL actually points, or put a proxy there.

scenarios.title: ss shows it listening, curl from the other subnet times out
scenarios.summary: Listening is not reachable. Localhost never hits INPUT the way eth0 does. Find the DROP.

scenarios.title: dig returns an address, curl hangs, ping6 is the thing that actually fails
scenarios.summary: AAAA without a routed v6 prefix is an outage. Query both families; curl -6 isolates the path.

scenarios.title: One client says NXDOMAIN, another says SERVFAIL, the name is in the zone file
scenarios.summary: NXDOMAIN is denial (often a rewritten question). SERVFAIL is 'I could not answer'. Read the QUESTION section.

scenarios.title: I updated the A record five minutes ago and this box still hits the old IP
scenarios.summary: dig talks to a nameserver; curl uses NSS. /etc/hosts and stub caches beat the zone.

scenarios.title: curl http:// works on my laptop and talks garbage in the cluster
scenarios.summary: Cleartext HTTP on a TLS port is a protocol mismatch. Health probes inherit this constantly.

scenarios.title: The host can ping its neighbour and cannot reach the internet
scenarios.summary: On-link success is not a default route. ip route get tells you before you debug TLS.

scenarios.title: Traceroute dies at hop 3, so they opened a change to replace the router — TCP still works
scenarios.summary: Stars are missing probe replies, not a down core. Believe TCP to the service port first.

scenarios.title: The router has two interfaces and packets die in the kernel
scenarios.summary: NAT rules do nothing if ip_forward is 0. tcpdump in without out is forwarding or FORWARD policy.

scenarios.title: The allow rule is in the list and the packet still dies
scenarios.summary: First match wins. Zero counters on your ACCEPT means an earlier DROP ate the flow.

scenarios.title: Packets leave with a private source and the next hop throws them away
scenarios.summary: Forwarding without SNAT leaks RFC1918 onto a network that will not route it back.

scenarios.title: The certificate is valid and curl still says the name does not match
scenarios.summary: Trust and identity are separate. Curl-by-IP and missing SNI pick the wrong name or vhost.

scenarios.title: openssl s_client says verify return code 0 and the browser still warns
scenarios.summary: If SAN is present, CN is not used. A pretty wildcard CN with the wrong SAN still fails.

scenarios.title: Short API calls work, the upload dies at 61 seconds every time
scenarios.summary: Failures clustered at 60s or 350s are a middlebox timer. Bypass the LB once to see whose clock.

scenarios.title: Public DNS has the right answer and the office still hits the old private IP
scenarios.summary: Same qname, two RRsets. Update the private view; public TTL will not save you.

scenarios.title: The ban hammer hit the load balancer, and attackers still get through
scenarios.summary: X-Forwarded-For is a claim. Honour it only from hops you own; TCP source is what the client cannot spoof.

scenarios.title: The UDP service is up and the load balancer keeps taking it out of rotation
scenarios.summary: UDP/53 is not TCP/53. Default TCP health checks empty a DNS pool that still answers dig.

scenarios.title: Pod-to-pod is fine, crossing the overlay dies at 1420-byte payloads — ICMP still works
scenarios.summary: Overlay MTU must be underlay minus encapsulation. Same-node traffic never hits VXLAN.

scenarios.title: dig @8.8.8.8 works, the office resolver returns SERVFAIL, the zone looks signed
scenarios.summary: SERVFAIL plus success with +cd is BOGUS until proven otherwise. Parent DS is outside your zone file.

scenarios.title: tcpdump sees SYN, SYN-ACK, then the client keeps retransmitting SYN
scenarios.summary: SYN-SENT vs SYN-RECV: both hosts are honest. Stateful firewalls and strict RPF need a symmetric path.

scenarios.title: New connections fail with timeout, established SSH sessions keep working
scenarios.summary: NEW vs ESTABLISHED split is a full NAT/conntrack table, not a WAN cut. Raise max and stop the leak.

scenarios.title: Chrome is instant, curl is instant, the mobile app hangs until it falls back to HTTP/2
scenarios.summary: HTTP/3 is UDP/443. Alt-Svc plus a TCP-only allowlist makes working HTTPS feel slow.

scenarios.title: Dual-stack clients wait two seconds before every request; IPv4-only clients do not
scenarios.summary: A working A does not save you from a blackholed AAAA. Happy Eyeballs turns it into latency.

scenarios.title: The server log has no request and the client got RST in the middle of TLS
scenarios.summary: TTL mismatch and an empty app log: the RST was injected. Two taps beat bouncing the JVM.

scenarios.title: DNS is anycast, some offices get a POP that still has yesterday's zone
scenarios.summary: One address, many machines. NSID tells you which POP; TCP on anycast resets on failover.

scenarios.title: iptables -L is empty, nft list looks fine, packets still vanish
scenarios.summary: Empty iptables is not no firewall on nftables or eBPF. Trace the skb; name the datapath.
